h1: The 6 Best SSD NAS for Fast File Access of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best SSD NAS for Fast Files: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six NAS enclosures that suit SSD storage, sorted by bays, CPU, networking speed and how well they handle flash drives.
summary: The UGREEN DXP4800 Plus is the best NAS for SSD storage because its Pentium Gold CPU and four bays can run an all-SSD array without bottlenecks. The Beelink ME Pro is the compact NVMe pick, the DXP2800 is the content creator's 2-bay, and the Synology DS925+ is the choice if you want to mix hard drives with SSD cache. The Asustor and DS223 are the budget entries.
intro: A fast SSD in a slow NAS is wasted money. The most common mistake is filling an enclosure with flash drives and then discovering the 1Gb network port, or a weak CPU, caps real file transfers at hard drive speed. The enclosure, not the drive, usually sets the ceiling.

These six enclosures were compared through their spec sheets and owner feedback on everyday use. We ranked them on SSD readiness, CPU headroom, network speed, bay count and value. All of them are sold without drives, so factor in storage on top of the enclosure price. Two similar UGREEN models were left out to avoid repeating the same advice.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DXP4800 Plus 4-Bay with Intel Pentium Gold CPU
products.verdict: The enclosure with the CPU and bays to run a true all-SSD array.
products.description:
The DXP4800 Plus is a 4-bay diskless NAS with an Intel Pentium Gold 8505 five core CPU. It supports an all-SSD configuration across all four bays and offers RAID 5 and RAID 10.

It ranks first because the CPU has the headroom to actually use flash storage, while the cheaper 2-bay models are more likely to bottleneck. The price puts it in the $500 and up bracket before you buy any drives, so it is not a bargain, but it is the most complete option.

Buy it if SSD primary storage is the goal and you want redundancy. Remember that no drives are included.
products.skipIf: You only need a small backup box.

products.name: Beelink ME Pro Mini PC NAS, 2 Hard Drive Bays + 3x M.2 SSD Slots
products.verdict: A small box with three M.2 slots and dual LAN.
products.description:
The Beelink ME Pro pairs an Intel N95 CPU and 12GB LPDDR5 memory with a 128GB M.2 PCIe 3.0 SSD. It has two hard drive bays plus three M.2 SSD slots in total, with dual LAN.

It ranks second because it is the best NVMe focused option in a small body, yet the N95 CPU is a step below the Pentium in the DXP4800 Plus. The included SSD and memory also mean you spend less on parts.

Choose it if you want a quiet, compact NAS with fast flash for active files. It is not meant for heavy multi-user work.
products.skipIf: You run virtual machines or serve many users.

products.name: UGREEN NAS DXP2800 2-Bay Enclosure for Content Creators
products.verdict: A mirrored 2-bay SSD NAS that keeps project files fast and safe.
products.description:
The DXP2800 is a 2-bay diskless enclosure that can run RAID 1 with two SSDs. UGREEN aims it at content creator workflows and prices it as a lower cost way into all-SSD storage, in the $200 to $500 band.

It ranks third because it matches the Plus's SSD friendliness at a lower price but has only two bays. Mirroring protects against a single drive failure at the cost of half your capacity.

Buy it if you edit video or photos and want fast, protected access to active projects. If you need more capacity, look at the 4-bay models.
products.idealFor: Creators wanting mirrored SSD project storage.
products.skipIf: You need more than two drives.

products.name: Synology DS925+ 4-Bay DiskStation (Diskless)
products.verdict: Mix big hard drives with SSD or NVMe cache and Synology's DSM.
products.description:
The DS925+ is a 4-bay diskless DiskStation that supports hybrid HDD and SSD or NVMe cache setups. It runs the Synology DSM platform and offers RAID 5 and RAID 10.

It ranks fourth because it favors a mixed approach instead of an all-SSD one. That is cheaper per terabyte and uses the software that many people consider the most polished, but cache is not the same as all-flash storage.

Choose it if you want lots of capacity with speed where it counts. It sits in the $500 and up bracket, so budget accordingly.
products.idealFor: Big capacity with targeted SSD speed.

products.name: Asustor Drivestor 2 Gen 2 AS1202T 2-Bay NAS (Diskless)
products.verdict: 2.5GbE on a budget, with a modest quad core CPU.
products.description:
The AS1202T is a 2-bay diskless NAS with a quad core 1.7GHz CPU, 1GB of DDR4 memory and 2.5GbE networking. It is positioned as an entry level personal cloud and 4K media server.

It ranks fifth because 1GB of memory and a modest CPU limit it for demanding work. The 2.5GbE port is the highlight, since it lets SSDs run faster than a standard gigabit link.

Buy it for a simple, low cost SSD ready NAS. Spending in the $100 to $200 range will not buy extensive features.
products.idealFor: Budget users wanting faster than gigabit links.
products.skipIf: You need to run many apps.

products.name: Synology DS223 2-Bay Diskless NAS for Home & Office Backup
products.verdict: A modest SSD upgrade path on a trusted software platform.
products.description:
The DS223 is a 2-bay diskless NAS aimed at home and office backup. It supports SATA SSD installation and uses the Synology DSM platform.

It ranks last because it is positioned as a backup box rather than a performance machine, so the SSD speed gain is modest. Synology's software is the reason to buy it over cheaper rivals.

It suits home offices that want reliable backup with an optional faster drive. It is not for demanding all-flash workloads.
products.idealFor: Reliable backup for a small office.

methodology.title: SSD readiness
methodology.description: We favored enclosures that explicitly support all-SSD or NVMe configurations.

methodology.title: CPU headroom
methodology.description: A faster CPU keeps a flash array from being bottlenecked.

methodology.title: Network speed
methodology.description: 2.5GbE and dual LAN ports ranked above a single gigabit port.

methodology.title: Bays and RAID
methodology.description: More bays and RAID options mean better capacity and protection.

methodology.title: Value
methodology.description: Enclosure price was weighed against capability, noting that drives are extra.

whatMatters.detail: A standard gigabit port tops out near 110 MB/s, which a single SSD can exceed several times over. A 2.5GbE port raises that limit, so fast drives can show their speed. Check the listing for a 2.5GbE or 10GbE port, and make sure your router and switch support it too.
The CPU handles RAID, file indexing and any apps you run. A weak chip can cap transfers even with fast drives. Look for the named processor and match it to how many people and tasks will use the NAS.

Some enclosures take 2.5 inch SATA SSDs in the main bays, and others add M.2 NVMe slots for cache or storage. Counting bays and slot types tells you how much flash you can add. Read the bay and M.2 lines in the listing.

RAID spreads data across drives for speed or protection. RAID 1 mirrors two drives, while RAID 5 survives one failure across several. Pick RAID based on how many drives you will use, and check the enclosure lists it.
Synology's DSM is widely regarded as polished and easy to use. Other vendors offer their own apps that vary in maturity. Weigh the software as much as the hardware when deciding.

howToChoose.intro: Match the enclosure to the storage you plan to buy.

cards.label: All-SSD
cards.text: Every file reads at flash speed but costs more per terabyte. Covered by the DXP4800 Plus and DXP2800.

cards.label: Hybrid cache
cards.text: Large hard drives with SSD or NVMe cache for hot files. Covered by the Synology DS925+.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to hybrid unless every file needs flash speed.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: RAID 1 or better, flash drives and a fast network link so timelines scrub smoothly.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The UGREEN DXP2800 runs RAID 1 with two SSDs and is aimed at creators.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Several people or apps hit the NAS at once. The UGREEN DXP4800 Plus has the CPU headroom.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only back up files. The Synology DS223 or Asustor Drivestor 2 Gen 2 is enough.

faq.q: Do these NAS units include drives?
faq.a: No. Every enclosure here is sold diskless, so add the price of SSDs or hard drives to your budget.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when building an SSD NAS?
faq.a: Ignoring the network. A gigabit port limits transfers to hard drive speeds, so check for 2.5GbE or faster.

faq.q: Is an SSD NAS worth it over a hard drive one?
faq.a: For active files and many small reads, yes. For bulk archive storage, hard drives are far cheaper per terabyte.

faq.q: How do I set up a NAS?
faq.a: Install your drives, connect it to your router, and follow the vendor setup app to create a volume. Choose a RAID level before you copy data.

faq.q: How do I keep a NAS healthy?
faq.a: Keep its software updated, watch drive health alerts, and keep a separate backup of important files.
No. RAID protects against a drive failure, not deletion or corruption. Keep a separate copy of important data.

finalTake: For fast file access, the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus is the NAS that will never be the bottleneck. The Beelink ME Pro is the compact NVMe pick and the DXP2800 suits creators on a smaller budget. Choose the Synology DS925+ if capacity matters more than all-flash speed, and remember that drives are an extra cost for every one of these.
